intro: Colchester, in Essex, has two readers' trees on our map, a couple of hundred metres apart near Clingoe Hill in Greenstead, on the east side of the town. One is a very large pedunculate oak standing alone in open grass, its short wide trunk hollowed and burred, which a reader puts at 600 centimetres round and about 300 years old. The other is a cedar of Lebanon whose lowest branches spread across the ground in a wide skirt of dark needles. Both came to us as readers' photographs.
meta_description: Two readers' trees near Clingoe Hill in Colchester: a very large oak and a spreading cedar of Lebanon, where they stand and what we know.

trees.name: The Oak of Clingoe Hill
trees.age_estimate: about 300 years, by a reader's estimate
trees.story:
A reader photographed a great pedunculate oak in an open field on Clingoe Hill in Greenstead, on the east side of Colchester. They gave a girth of 600 centimetres and an age of about 300 years.

The photograph shows a tree that fills the frame. The crown is a full, rounded dome of dark green leaves, and under it a short, wide trunk with deep hollows and burrs at head height. Two people stand at its foot, one with arms spread wide against the bark, and they look small. The grass around it is dry and pale, the crown still green, so the picture was taken in a dry late summer.

We found no register entry or survey for this oak, so the girth and the age are the reader's figures. A girth of six metres is large for a pedunculate oak.

If you stand with your arms out against it, you can tell us how many hugs it takes.
trees.how_to_recognise: A huge domed oak standing alone in open dry grass, its short wide trunk hollowed and burred, with a few trees behind it.

trees.name: The Cedar near Clingoe Hill

location.address: Near Clingoe Hill, Greenstead, Colchester, Essex

trees.story:
A couple of hundred metres from the great oak on Clingoe Hill, on the east side of Colchester, stands this cedar. It was sent to us by the same reader who photographed that oak in its autumn leaf, and they know it as a cedar of Lebanon.

Cedars of Lebanon have been planted in English parks since the seventeenth century, and given room they grow into one of the grandest shapes a tree can take. In the photograph the trunk divides low into several great limbs, and these sweep out and up in long curves, tier above tier, carrying flat dark plates of foliage. The lowest branches have come right down and spread across the ground, so the tree seems to stand in a pool of its own needles, with mown grass and a path beyond. A second picture shows a branch up close, short tufts of blue-green needles and pale green cones standing upright on the twigs like candles.

The reader came back with figures of their own, a girth of about 555 centimetres and an age of about 155 years by their estimate. We have found no survey or planting record to set beside them, so if you know its history, tell us here.

Walk round to where the low branches meet the grass and look up through the arches of the limbs.
trees.how_to_recognise: A broad cedar whose trunk splits low into great curving limbs in tiers, its lowest branches lying along the ground in a wide skirt of dark needles, mown grass and a path behind it.
trees.access: The reader photographed it from mown grass beside a path. We found no published access terms for the ground, so follow any signs.

question_meta: A very large oak and a spreading cedar stand near Clingoe Hill in Colchester. Where they are and what readers say about them.
question_answer: A reader found a very large pedunculate oak (Quercus robur) on Clingoe Hill, Greenstead, Colchester, with a girth of about 600 cm and an age of about 300 years by their estimate.
question_context: Everything this page says comes from readers' photographs and figures, sent through the app. The oak stands alone in open grass on Clingoe Hill in Greenstead, on the east side of Colchester; the first reader's own label placed it near Mistley, about ten kilometres away, so we have put it where it stands. We found no register entry or published survey for it, so the girth of about 600 centimetres and the age of about 300 years are the reader's. Its photographs show a rounded crown over a short trunk with deep hollows and burrs at head height. A couple of hundred metres to the east, a second reader photographed a cedar of Lebanon whose trunk splits low into curving limbs and whose lowest branches lie along the grass. We have no girth or age for the cedar yet. We found no published terms for access to either piece of ground, so follow any signs. If you have measured a trunk or know a tree's history, tell us on its page and it goes into this answer.

faq.q: Which trees are on the map in Colchester?
faq.a: A very large pedunculate oak (Quercus robur) on Clingoe Hill and a cedar of Lebanon (Cedrus libani) a couple of hundred metres to its east.
Near Clingoe Hill, Greenstead, on the east side of Colchester.
A reader gave a girth of about 600 centimetres. We have found no survey to compare.
